Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Helix likes the performance profile for 4xA100 equivalent clusters. We are starting procurement conversations and have two specific asks that will determine whether we go with a multi‑site on‑prem roll or a hosted hybrid approach: 

1) Platform fee amortization: our finance team would prefer to amortize the flat platform fee over 36 months and treat it as CAPEX rather than an immediate OPEX hit. Is Redwood able to provide an invoice / SOW structure or language that supports amortization for accounting teams? Are there constraints (minimum term, non‑refundability, transferability between sites)?

2) Tiered burst credits: Helix expects seasonal spikes (clinical reports processing). Can we structure a pool of "burst credits" that are consumed only during high‑load windows (billed as token or node equivalents) and that expire quarterly? Ideally those credits would be cheaper than on‑demand overruns and count against committed capacity before any overage.

Attached is a draft SOW and our initial capacity profile. Also copying our procurement lead Emily who will coordinate PO terms.

High level ask: sample commercial language we can present to our CFO and an estimate for amortization-friendly invoicing + an example burst credit construct.

Hi Sanjay — great to hear you and the team liked the demo. Short answers up front, longer details below:

- Amortization: Yes, we can support invoice structures that customers typically amortize (term‑bound platform fee with milestone invoicing or a single upfront invoice). We can provide contract language that clarifies non‑transferability across legal entities without an amendment, but can allow site reallocation within the same legal entity for a modest admin fee.
- Burst credits: We offer a tiered burst credit SKU that can be (a) pre‑purchased and banked for a quarter, or (b) purchased as a discounted overage bucket that applies only after committed capacity is consumed. Credits typically expire at quarter end unless otherwise agreed.

Details (for CFO / procurement):

1) Suggested amortization-friendly constructs:
- 36‑month amortization example: platform fee = $540,000 (annualized $180k) — invoice options: upfront, 3x annual, or quarterly milestone. We can issue a revenue recognition schedule and a SOW addendum that ties the fee to license entitlement and support SLA.
- Contract language considerations: specify non‑refundable unless termination for cause; allow accounting-friendly milestone invoicing; include a clause for site reallocation within the same legal entity.

2) Burst credit constructs we recommend:
- Pooled quarterly credits: buy X credits for Q, used by any site in the entitlemed cluster, expire at quarter close. Discount vs on‑demand: typically 20–30% off spot.
- Committed + overflow slab: committed baseline (nodes/token budget) priced at an anchor rate; overflow billed from a pre‑purchased discounted slab until exhausted, then on‑demand.

Next steps: I can produce: (a) sample SOW wording and invoice templates for 36‑month amortization, and (b) a short pricing appendix showing committed vs burst credit math for your Q4 estimates. I have an internal pricing model I can attach.

Looping in Marissa (commercial ops) and Rishi (legal pricing consult) to review the sample language and confirm whether we can offer a time‑bound (quarterly) credit expiry exception for large deals.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Team — quick legal / revenue ops guidance:

1) Amortization language: we will provide a SOW addendum that explicitly defines the platform fee as a license entitlement billed on schedule X. Important callouts: non‑transferability across distinct legal entities w/out amendment; right to reclaim entitlements on early termination (pro‑rata refund only in narrow, pre‑approved circumstances). That should satisfy CFOs who want to capitalize. I suggest the 36‑month schedule be represented in the SOW as an exhibit showing milestone dates and invoice amounts.

2) Burst credits: limit contractual exposure by capping the maximum quarterly extension we allow (one time) and specifying that credits expire at quarter close unless a written amendment is signed. For high‑value deals we can offer a tailored expiry and deeper discounts, but escalate to VP approval for >$1.5M platform fee.
